screen: The phone remote: a web page opened on the volunteer's own phone (about 360 points wide, one hand, often in the dark), joined to the operator computer over the church's wireless network. The big controls are at the bottom; a row of four tabs sits under them. More tab: message to the room, countdown, language and keys blocks. A paragraph in the last block.
moment: The person looks for a key on the computer.
does: Lists, in one short paragraph, the keys that work on this page when a keyboard is attached. The Space bar and also the arrow pointing down go one slide forward; the arrow pointing up goes one slide back; the slash key opens the search; C jumps to the chorus, V to the verse after this one, B to the bridge; a digit from 1 to 9 jumps to that part of the song; F1 hides the words, F2 makes the screen black, F3 shows the logo, F6 switches the projector on or off.
register: The page speaks to a volunteer holding a phone at the console or standing beside the stage: any age, no time to read, thumb-sized buttons. Plain, short, polite and familiar. No honorifics, no jargon.
notes: Key names stay as printed on the keyboard. Every key in the list above must be named, and no other. It is a paragraph that wraps over several lines on the phone, so write whole short sentences; no slashes standing in for words.
